newsitem.title: UK: Crocodile fillets tempt meat-loving Britons.
newsitem.headline: Crocodile fillets tempt meat-loving Britons.

text.p: Crocodile meat will be on sale for the first time next week in British supermarkets, joining ostrich and buffalo in an exotic range of fare tempting shoppers away from traditional beef and lamb.
Supermarket chain Sainsbury's said it was buying crocodile fillets from Australia for sale as an experiment in seven of its stores.
"We already sell buffalo and ostrich. People are getting more adventurous in their tastes," a spokeswoman said on Saturday.

British meat lovers have turned increasingly to unusual alternatives to beef steaks following the scare over mad cow disease and its possible link to the fatal human brain-wasting condition Creutzfeldt Jakob Disease.
Ostrich and buffalo were introduced to selected supermarkets last year and kangaroo meat appeared in some stores in September.
